extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians and mathematical-sciences authors (students through faculty); instructors of transferable-skills courses; authors preparing talks, papers, books, or blogs in mathematics
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and practical standards for writing, typesetting, indexing, and publishing in the mathematical sciences, covering prose, LaTeX practice, workflow, talks, reviewing, and bibliography preparation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logical organization and reference usability
rubrics_metrics.description: Reorganize material in a logical way that makes the book easier to use for reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure chapters and sections so readers can quickly find practical advice; prioritize a layout suitable for both linear reading and reference lookups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design and formatting quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Improve design and formatting to make the text more readable and to make more efficient use of the page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use conciser lists, considered typography and layout choices; revise formatting choices from older editions to match modern standards and improve readability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep advice up to date with publishing developments
rubrics_metrics.description: Reflect recent developments in publishing (open access, DOIs, ORCID, etc.) and modern workflows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remove obsolete procedures (e.g., submitting hard-copy manuscripts) and add guidance on current practices such as including DOIs and ORCID IDs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Workflow and automation
rubrics_metrics.description: Organize and automate the many tasks involved in writing using efficient tools and practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make efficient use of text editors, markup languages, plain-text tools, spellcheckers, version control, and other automation to manage writing tasks and digital materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of modern LaTeX packages and typesetting practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt current useful LaTeX packages and typesetting knowledge to produce higher-quality documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples given include using enumitem for better list formatting, booktabs for tables, listings for syntax highlighting, and Beamer for talks; update package advice as packages evolve.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concise, well-formatted lists (use enumitem)
rubrics_metrics.description: Format numbered and bulleted lists using enumitem to produce more concise lists that make better use of the page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer compact list layouts and consistent list styling; the author notes switching all lists to enumitem for improved concision and page usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tables: minimize rules and use booktabs
rubrics_metrics.description: Minimize the use of table rules (lines) and use the booktabs package for better-looking tables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer less-cluttered table designs with appropriate spacing and rule usage as advocated by booktabs; see author's blog post for rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Slides and talks: use Beamer and examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Illustrate and encourage use of the Beamer package when preparing talks and slides.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concrete slide examples and syntax-highlighted listings for slides; use color thoughtfully for readability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of color for syntax highlighting and slides
rubrics_metrics.description: Use color to highlight code listings and slide examples where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply color for clarity in listings and slide examples while considering accessibility and print/readability concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indexing: prepare a good index
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide instruction on creating an effective index and emphasize indexing as an important but infrequently practiced skill.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a chapter on Preparing an Index that explains indexing techniques and best practices; build a better index by studying indexing literature and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bibliography practices: backref, DOIs and URLs
rubrics_metrics.description: Use backref in the bibliography to point back to pages where entries are cited and include DOIs/URLs in the online bibliography.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make bibliographic entries more useful by enabling back-references and adding DOIs/URL links in online/bbl/PDF bibliography files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remove outdated/duplicative appendices
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid including appendices or content that are now redundant because the information is readily available online.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: remove long appendices listing prize winners or organization addresses when such information is available on the web.

rubrics_metrics.name: English usage: address common pitfalls
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat specific English usage topics explicitly (Zombie Nouns, Double Negatives, Serial/Oxford Comma, Split Infinitives).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide guidance and examples on these usage points to help mathematical writers produce clearer prose and be aware of stylistic choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sidebars for related brief topics
rubrics_metrics.description: Use sidebars (gray boxes) to give brief diversions on topics related to the main text, such as 'Publication Peculiarities'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deploy short, focused asides to cover peripheral or illustrative information without interrupting main exposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapters for different writing forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Include dedicated chapters covering different forms of mathematical communication (writing a blog post, refereeing and reviewing, writing a book, preparing an index, workflow).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide form-specific advice recognizing that blogs, reviews, books and talks have distinct conventions and requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refereeing and reviewing practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Offer guidance on how to referee and review mathematical work effectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a chapter on refereeing and reviewing that discusses standards and practicalities of peer review in mathematics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make the book usable as a course text for transferable skills
rubrics_metrics.description: Design material so it can be used in transferable-skills modules across mathematics departments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize chapters and examples to support classroom teaching and self-study for students and early-career researchers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical editing and copy-edit collaboration
rubrics_metrics.description: Work with professional copy editors and adopt publisher style where appropriate to improve clarity and conform to SIAM/other style guides.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collaboration with a copy editor can find many improvements and teach authors about publisher-specific style conventions; consult AMS Author Handbook, SIAM Style Manual, Chicago Manual of Style as needed.
